learning_objective: The learner will attribute the main cause of a team's difficulty in each of six short vignettes to one of five causes, correctly attributing at least five of six on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** why-is-this-team-stuck
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** attribute
**Learning Objective:** The learner will attribute the main cause of a team's difficulty in each of six short vignettes to one of five causes, correctly attributing at least five of six on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** shared goals, team roles, individual accountability, active listening, conflict resolution (all defined in this chapter above this block and in the section "Communication Skills" below). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 6 vignettes, the learner selects the main cause and submits it. A selection is correct when it matches the "Main cause" column in Content. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the cause definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A struggling team lacks knowledge or effort. (2) The quiet member is the problem. (3) Every team problem is a conflict. **Instructional Rationale:** Attributing a cause requires reading the details of a situation and separating similar-looking symptoms, such as silence from unclear roles versus silence from unresolved conflict. Single-cause vignettes with plausible distractors make the learner look for the defining clue. **Content:** Five causes with definitions shown on request: | Cause | Definition shown | |---|---| | Unclear shared goal | Members are working toward different or vague outcomes | | Unclear roles | No one knows who is responsible for what | | No individual accountability | One or more members can avoid doing their part without anyone noticing | | Poor listening | Members talk past each other or do not take in what others say | | Unresolved conflict | A disagreement is being avoided or has become personal | Six vignettes: | # | Vignette shown to the learner | Main cause | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Half the team is building a poster and half is writing a survey, and each thinks the other half is wasting time. | Unclear shared goal | The two halves are working toward different outcomes. | | 2 | Four students each start the same task, while two other tasks sit untouched, because nobody was asked to take them. | Unclear roles | No one knows who owns which task. | | 3 | The team's report is excellent, but only one student wrote it and the others did not contribute, and the teacher cannot tell. | No individual accountability | A member can hide behind the group's output. | | 4 | When Priya suggests a change, Dev repeats his earlier idea as if she had not spoken. | Poor listening | Dev is not taking in what Priya says. | | 5 | Maya and Jordan have stopped talking after an argument about who copied whose idea, and the rest of the team is avoiding the topic. | Unresolved conflict | An argument has become personal and is being avoided. | | 6 | The team agreed to "do something about food waste," but when it is time to choose, no two members can say what success would look like. | Unclear shared goal | The goal is too vague to share. | **Provenance:** The causes follow the chapter sections on collaboration, communication, and conflict resolution. The vignettes are illustrative, written for this chapter. **Rules:** Each vignette has exactly one main cause, given in Content. A vignette is scored on its first submitted cause only. The score counts first-attempt correct causes out of 6. Mastery is a score >= 5. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads one vignette and sees the five causes. 2. The learner selects a cause and submits it. The sim marks it correct or incorrect and shows the feedback text. 3. If incorrect, the learner may choose again; the second attempt does not change the score. After the second attempt, the correct cause and reason are shown. 4. After all 6 vignettes, the sim shows the score. 5. The learner should notice that vignettes 1 and 6 share a cause although they look different, and that no vignette is solved by working harder. **Feedback:** 6 vignettes, shuffled once per session, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: [cause]. [Why text]." Incorrect: "Not quite. [Why text for the correct answer, without naming the cause]." After the second attempt the correct cause is revealed and the vignette counts as missed. A running score "First-try correct: n of 6" is shown. Final message for a score >= 5: "You can find the real reason a team is stuck." For a score < 5: "Review the five causes and try again; the vignettes will be reshuffled." **Starting State:** Vignette 1 of the shuffled order is shown with the five causes, the score "First-try correct: 0 of 6," and the prompt "What is the main reason this team is stuck?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter names the structural elements of a good team as shared goals, team roles, individual accountability, listening, and conflict handling. The food-waste team is the running example. The mastery bar is 5 of 6.
